bull.b: A rapid, high-volume launch with accelerating new patient starts and materially upgraded full-year guidance demonstrates durable commercial adoption and prescriber penetration. Sustained quarterly starts and strong launch metrics indicate lasting revenue base potential as the product moves from early uptake to steady-state sales.

Very high and improving product gross margins reflect favorable product economics and improving gross-to-net dynamics. Durable margin strength provides operating leverage as revenue scales, improving the company’s ability to fund R&D and SG&A without proportional margin erosion over the medium term.

bull.t: Stronger balance sheet and cash runway
bull.b: Material deleveraging and a sizeable cash position reduce solvency risk and extend runway to execute launches and Phase III programs. Lower net debt and positive equity provide strategic flexibility to invest in commercialization and trials while targeting cash‑flow positivity without near‑term capital raises.

bear.t: Heavy cash burn and negative free cash flow
bear.b: Large negative operating and free cash flows create persistent runway pressure despite current cash balances. Continued high cash burn from launches and Phase III programs risks requiring additional financing or cutbacks if commercial uptake or reimbursement outcomes slow, making sustainability conditional on execution.

Even with accelerating revenue, operating and net losses are severe enough to keep returns strongly negative. Achieving durable profitability requires sustained scale, controlled SG&A/R&D growth, and preservation of gross margins; failure on any front prolongs cash consumption and delays breakeven.

Revenue outlook depends on favorable payer access, regulatory approvals, and stable GTN trends. European payer constraints, potential GTN increases, milestone obligations, and optimistic uptake assumptions create structural execution risk that could materially reduce net realized revenue and slow path to self-funded growth.
